revision_agent_roles.title: The agent chooses; the tool executes a capability
revision_agent_roles.caption: Original teaching abstraction for diagnosing a frozen base case v43. An LLM agent chooses a tool call, the callable interface runs against the case and solver, and returned evidence informs the next choice. LangGraph is shown as a possible orchestration runtime for state and execution, not as a grid solver or a claim about a particular PowerAgent implementation.
revision_agent_roles.assumptions: The v43 case, run_pf(v43, base) interface and feedback fields are illustrative; no tool was executed and no numerical outcome is asserted. Tool and agent name interface/decision roles; a tool may internally wrap another agent or a complex service. The outer framework marker does not establish the correctness of any electrical result. No PowerAgent SDK relationship is claimed.
revision_agent_roles.source_locator: Russell/Norvig Section 2.1; Anthropic 'What are agents?' and 'Agents'; official LangGraph overview and Tools opening definitions.

revision_powerdag_gate.title: Check the prerequisite before executing a state-dependent tool
revision_powerdag_gate.caption: Original teaching adaptation of PowerDAG v4, Section IV-C, PDF p.5. A planner proposes a voltage-violation check. A prerequisite gate blocks execution and returns the missing solve to the planner when the required solved network state is unavailable; otherwise the check proceeds. This is neither exact source code nor the complete/minimal workflow DAG.
revision_powerdag_gate.assumptions: The v43 identifier and call wording are illustrative. The figure strengthens the teaching condition to a solution for the current named network. The paper's formal supervisor tests required Write-tool names against executed-tool names; do not infer from that alone a version-aware freshness/invalidation guarantee. Rule coverage is curated rather than exhaustive, and unruled tools remain executable. A blocked call leaves environment state unchanged; passing this prerequisite is not a numerical feasibility or safety proof.
revision_powerdag_gate.source_locator: Section IV-C, PDF p.5, voltage-violation example and Eqs. (8)-(10); Algorithm 1. Figure 2, PDF p.3, locates the supervisor between planner and executor.
